speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning. To understand the severity of your double vision and weakness, do you notice any slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or drooping on one side of your face?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Creatine_Kinase

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your normal blood work and the combination of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, have you noticed if your double vision worsens when you look to the side or down?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies, Anti-MuSK_Antibodies

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated), Anti-MuSK_Antibodies: Not Detected

speaker: Doctor
text:
Excellent, the positive Acetylcholine Receptor antibodies strongly confirm Myasthenia Gravis. Since you also have upper limb weakness and trouble with stairs, do you experience significant fatigue in your muscles after brief periods of activity, or is the weakness constant?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_CT: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected; Chest_X-Ray: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood work and antibody tests confirm Myasthenia Gravis, but your chest imaging rules out a thymoma, do you experience worsening of your double vision or limb weakness specifically toward the end of the day or after physical exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis (Ocular and Limb-involving, Thymoma-negative).
